<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
For the Diophantine equations
$$
F_n+F_m=2^a \quad \text{and} \quad F_n^2+F_m^2=2^a,
$$
the equations are symmetric in the variables $n$ and $m$. Therefore, without loss of generality, one may assume that $n\ge m$. In contrast, the equation
$$
F_n^2+F_m=2^a
$$
is not symmetric, since the roles of $n$ and $m$ are fundamentally different. Consequently, we have to treat the two cases $n\ge m$ and $m>n$ separately.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{Thm1}
The Diophantine equation \eqref{eq1} has the following solutions in nonnegative integers $n,m,a$:
\begin{align*}
   \left( n,m,a\right) \in \big\{ &(1,0,0),(1,1,1),(2,0,0),(2,1,1),(2,2,1),(3,0,2),(6,0,6), (0,1,0), (0,2,0),
\\ &(0,3,1), (0,6,3), (1,4,2),(4,10,6), (1, 2, 1), (2, 4, 2) \big\}. 
\end{align*}
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{Thm2}
Assume that $\gamma _{1},\gamma _{2},...,\gamma _{r}$ are
positive real algebraic numbers in a real algebraic number field $\mathbb{K}$
of degree $D$, $b_{1},b_{2},\ldots,b_{r}\in \mathbb{Z}$, and 
$$\Lambda :=\gamma _{1}^{b_{1}}...\gamma _{r}^{b_{r}}-1 $$ 
is not zero. Then 
$$|\Lambda |>\exp \left( -1.4\cdot 30^{r+3}\cdot r^{4.5}\cdot D^{2}(1+\log
D)(1+\log B)A_{1}A_{2}...A_{r}\right) , 
$$ 
where 
$$
B\geq \max \left\{ |b_{1}|,...,|b_{r}|\right\} , 
$$ 
and 
$$A_{i}\geq \max \left\{ Dh(\gamma _{i}),|\log \gamma _{i}|,0.16\right\}\quad \text{for all } i=1,...,r. $$
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{Lem1}Let $M$ be a positive integer, let $p/q$ be a convergent of the
continued fraction expansion of the irrational number $\gamma $ such that $q>6M,$ and
let $A,B,\mu $ be some real numbers with $A>0$ and $B>1.$ Let $\epsilon
:=||\mu q||-M||\gamma q||.$ If $\epsilon >0,$ then there exists no solution
to the inequality 
$$
0<|u\gamma -v+\mu |<AB^{-w}, 
$$
in positive integers $u,v,$ and $w$ with 
$$
u\leq M\text{ and }w\geq \frac{\log (Aq/\epsilon )}{\log B}. 
$$
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lemma2.3}
For all $n \ge 1$, we have 
$$
\nu_2(F_n)=
\begin{cases}
0, & \text{if } n \equiv 1,2 \pmod{3},\\[4pt]
1, & \text{if } n \equiv 3 \pmod{6},\\[4pt]
3, & \text{if } n \equiv 6 \pmod{12},\\[4pt]
\nu_2(n)+2, & \text{if } n \equiv 0 \pmod{12}.
\end{cases}
$$
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
